findings.title: Use a valid iOS WebView scheme
findings.why_it_matters: The packaged iOS app will be configured to load its bundled WebView content from `Lá Lành://localhost`, but that value is not a valid URL scheme: it contains non-ASCII characters and a space. URL construction rejects this value, so Capacitor cannot form the local content URL and the app can fail to load its interface. Replacing it with an ASCII scheme such as `la-lanh` preserves the display name while giving the WebView a valid origin.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `ios.scheme` to an ASCII URL scheme such as `la-lanh`, then run Capacitor sync and launch a Release build to confirm the bundled WebView opens at `la-lanh://localhost` and native API requests still pass their CSRF/origin checks.
evidence: The synced iOS configuration reproduces this unchanged as `"scheme": "Lá Lành"`; a URL parser rejects `Lá Lành://localhost` because URL schemes must use ASCII letters, digits, `+`, `-`, and `.` after the initial letter.

testing_gaps: Native iOS toolchain was unavailable: archive and launch the Release app to verify the privacy manifest is bundled, WebView debugging remains disabled, and the local WebView starts successfully after the scheme correction.
Exercise a real HTTPS API session on an iOS device or simulator: create/resume the cookie-backed guest session, persist the non-auth CSRF token, and complete a mutation after relaunch.
